formal.anchor: Once Step 291/next operator-discovery work is complete, the Kernel can be decomposed into C3 components. Potentially: State Manager, Discrimination Engine (Buddhi hypothesis), Transformation Engine, Evidence Evaluator, Relation Manager, Qualification/Zero, Provenance Manager, Invariant Validator. But I would not yet call these canonical C3 components. ... Buddhi != Transformation ... Qualification != Rejection ... Zero != EmptyKnowledge. These distinctions could fundamentally change the eventual C3 decomposition.

governance.anchor: C3 -- Knowledge Kernel Component Diagram ... Knowledge Kernel: State Manager, Discrimination Engine (Buddhi hypothesis), Transformation Engine, Qualification Engine (Zero hypothesis), Evidence Evaluator, Relation Engine, Invariant Validator, Provenance/Transition Recorder. lexical.anchor: Knowledge Kernel -- the bounded mechanism responsible for evaluating candidate epistemic transformations and maintaining the transition from K_t to K_{t+1}, subject to KnowledgeOS invariants. Inside it we currently do not freeze: Buddhi, Sattva, Rajas, Tamas, Acquire, Compare, Qualify, Derive, Revise, Purify, Moksha... Those are still candidate concepts/operators discovered through the Gītā lens and mathematical research.

rationale_evidence.anchor: the Kernel is a C2 container -- C1 System Context, C2 Container, Kernel as a C2 container. A DDD/architecture placement claim, and it is T2 at best. 291 established that O membership, equiv, Qualify and delta are all open -- a container boundary presupposes knowing what is inside it. The project's C4 rule also binds: C4 views are documentation only; frozen artifacts win on conflict. Recorded, not adopted. A-Q1.
